newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Air Ukraine to choose Western partner next month.
newsitem.headline: Air Ukraine to choose Western partner next month.

text.p: Ukrainian airline Air Ukraine will decide next month whether to opt for Europe or America to replace its ageing Soviet-era fleet, a senior company official said Friday.
But plans to choose this month between Boeing Co. and Eruope's Airbus Industrie have come to nothing.
"The situation is not clear at all. There is complete silence on the issue," the official said.

The plans to lease or buy Western-made planes are part of a project by the state-owned airline to meet demand in the former Soviet republic, which has lifted Soviet-era travel restrictions and allowed people to go abroad.
"The Ukrainian aviation market is growing and has amazing prospects," a transport ministry official said, noting that business travel and tourism were both on the upswing.
"In the coming decade Ukraine's needs will stand at several dozen Western-made planes."

Air Ukraine, which in 1991 inherited planes left on its territory by Soviet flag-carrier Aeroflot after the collapse of Soviet Union, has a fleet of 240 planes, mostly Soviet-made Tupolev 154 and 134s, Antonov 24s and Yakovlev 40 and 42s. It also flies one Boeing 737.
But more than half the Soviet-made planes are grounded and Air Ukraine started its search for a Western partner this year.

The airline said in July it would choose Boeing for trans-Atlantic routes from 1997. Two months later it said it would lease Airbus planes, and Airbus Industrie began conducting demonstration flights over Kiev.

The airline now flies to New York and Toronto with Soviet-made Il-62 jets, and it plans non-stop flights to Chicago and Washington soon, adding Los Angeles and Miami by 1999. It also serves Ukraine, the former Soviet Union, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, India and China.
